summary: Malpeque range lights on Fish Island, lit since 1853 at the entrance to Malpeque Bay. The 1961 rear tower was discontinued in 2011; the old front tower is restored at Cabot Beach Provincial Park.

light.note: A light on Fish Island from 1853 (LighthouseFriends: 'likely went into operation' in early summer 1853). Replaced by a new light and range in 1877. The metal rear range tower dates from 1961 and was discontinued in 2011. The range is not on the Coast Guard list of lights (modified 2026-08-25).

range_lights.note: Front and rear range lights. Rear: metal skeletal tower with wooden upper portion, 15.2 m (50 ft), erected 1961; discontinued 2011. Front: the old wooden front range tower, cut in two and moved to Cabot Beach Provincial Park in 1989.

events.note: Light on Fish Island, probably lit early summer 1853 (LighthouseFriends). Keeper paid from 16 June 1853.
Second Fish Island light built by hired labour, with £100 appropriated in 1857 and set going in August 1857 (LighthouseFriends).
New white square wooden light and range light put into operation at the opening of navigation in 1877 (LighthouseFriends; PEI LHS).
Range light moved 6 m (20 ft) south to clear a bank (LighthouseFriends).
Range light moved again, to clear a sand spit off Darnley Point (LighthouseFriends).
Red range light on a mast marks the entrance to Darnley Basin; in service until 1897 (LighthouseFriends).
Oil shed erected at the station, $175, by day labour (Marine report, year to June 1906).
Repairs to the Fish Island tower (Marine report, year to June 1907).
35 mm Diamond vapour installation and adjustable brass stand replace the duplex lamp of the main light (Marine report, year to June 1909).
Metal skeletal rear range tower erected (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett; PEI LHS).
Front range tower, eroded, cut in two and moved by helicopter to Cabot Park, where it was reassembled (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).
Coast Guard discontinues the metal rear range tower (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett 'inactive since 2011').
Reported that the rear tower was no longer on the island (LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and the Society both put the new light and range into service in 1877. The Society also gives a 1913 date for a fourth light and 'circa 1913' for the restored front tower, which the story does not adopt: Marine reports show repairs to the Fish Island tower in 1907. The story gives 1877 and notes the 1913 date.
Rowlett gives the Fish Island front range tower as 7 m (23 ft); the Society gives 14 m (46 ft) for the Cabot Park tower. The story gives no height for it.
LighthouseFriends gives John Craig 1859-1867 and the Society 1859-1865. LighthouseFriends and the Society give Peter Hickey 1913-1924. The story follows LighthouseFriends and notes the differences.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on several dates; the story says so where it matters. (1) Keeper table, Marine 1910 (scan p. 255, printed p. 253): the Gould line is clean OCR and was used; 'Fish Island Patrick Gould Dec. 7, 1906' is matched by position on one line, so it is reasonably safe. (2) The Marine 1917-18 keeper table prints 'Malpeque John Hickey May 8. 1915', which conflicts with LighthouseFriends and the Society (Peter Hickey, 1913 start). Not reconciled; an editor should check the page image before publication. (3) The Marine 1910 and 1909 tables also list a 'Malpeque' station keeper 'J. Champion', appointed 10 December 1896. This is probably a different station (the Darnley or Malpeque lights), not Fish Island, and it is not used. (4) The Marine 1902-1903 tables name 'Sinclair, Wm' with Fish Island, and print an appointment date for Fish Island of 8 March 1897 at a column position that cannot be matched with certainty; not used. (5) Fish Island is also a Nova Scotia light station in the same Marine reports (Argyle); only the PEI section is used. (6) The 1907 repairs line prints its amount as '288 36', which is not used. (7) The record's characteristic (Iso W 2s), focal height (17.0 m) and range (10 nm) cannot be checked: the Coast Guard list has no range light here, and the Wikipedia lead gives 16.8 m focal height (not cited). (8) The record's coordinates (46.578099, -63.720314) sit near Wikipedia's and about 1 km from LighthouseFriends' rear-range point. (9) Front range tower height: Rowlett 7 m, the Society 14 m; not stated in the story. (10) The Society's 1913 date for a 'fourth Fish Island Lighthouse' conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 1876-77 date and with the 1907 and 1909 Marine entries; see resolved_conflicts. (11) The Darnley Point range is a different station (Malpeque Outer Range) and is not covered here. (12) Chronicling America searches for 'Malpeque' with 'light' returned nothing relevant. (13) 1989 volunteers are named only by their roles, as they are living people. (14) The Cabot Park tower's reconstruction year is not given consistently; the story says it was reassembled there in 1989. Checker pass (2026-10-28): the 1910 Gould row (Dec. 7, 1906) was confirmed on the archive.org page image (scan p. 255, printed p. 253). The 1906 oil shed, 1907 repairs and 1909 Main Light entries were checked under their 'Prince Edward Island' headings in the stored text, and the 1912 'Fish island range' line is in the PEI list. The story now says the 1851 gale date comes from the Society (footnote 2), that the light stood (not stands) from 1853, and that the anchorage duty was 'said to be' for lights, as the source's 'purportedly' requires. Removed: 'The entrance was the difficulty' (no source) and 'which fits the 2011 discontinuance' (an inference the list does not state).
